description: Stage only: code.json, plus the one row a stage carries and production does not. On test stages the database connection reads the pool database command's outcome (src/pool/database.ts), so it waits on that command's re-run.

values.name: EXECUTOR_TELEMETRY
values.why: A secret: the telemetry settings with their credential, and beside them the release's build version, which differs on every release. Only that one field may differ. A changed endpoint or credential in it refuses, like any other secret.

codeOnly.why: The release ships main as a whole. Holding the bulk-import store's Worker at older code while the pool Worker and the history schema move is version skew, so its code moves with the rest. Only its code. The rule: every property, setting and binding of this Worker is the same in the plan as in State, in the last finished generation and, after an interrupted apply, in the unfinished one as well, whatever the plan calls the row; either may be what is live. Three exceptions. Its entry file may sit under another checkout's directory. A setting named under values may differ in its named fields, in the setting and in the binding that carries it. For a setting named under references, State may hold an older copy of its resource, and the plan holds the resource as State records it now, or the resource itself while that updates; this holds only while its one binding holds one wire entry that the upload carries, named after the setting and as State has it. That binding alone may differ in the copy of a database connection's origin that local development reads, which no upload carries. Anything else refuses here. Its upload must also carry the serving version's bindings and no migration (wire.fixedBindings), so its Durable Object classes and their stored jobs stay as they are. The Worker has three more bindings that are not settings of its own: the two source stores and the vault bucket. They are named in neither list, so a refusal that names one of them, or any other binding, means one of two things. Either what this Worker is attached to really changed, which is not a healing release's to carry: ship it in a normal release. Or an earlier release that was updating that bucket or store stopped at this Worker, and State's unfinished copy of the binding lacks a value that was not known then: finish that release first. This check does not guess which; it refuses both.
